/-!
# Conjecture 9.1

by R. B. J. T. Allenby

A group is potent if, for every element and every positive integer dividing its
order, there is a finite homomorphic image in which the element has precisely
that order. Is the free product of two potent groups again potent?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.1»

/-- A group $G$ is potent if, for every $x \in G$ and every positive integer
$n$ dividing the order of $x$, there is a surjective homomorphism from $G$ to a
finite group under which the image of $x$ has order exactly $n$.

Here `orderOf x = 0` means that $x$ has infinite order, so every positive
integer divides `orderOf x` in this case. -/
def IsPotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : G) (n : ℕ), n ≠ 0 → n ∣ orderOf x →
    ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Group Q) (_ : Finite Q) (f : G →* Q),
      Function.Surjective f ∧ orderOf (f x) = n

/--
Is the free product of two potent groups again potent?
-/

theorem kourovka.«9.1» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G H : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Group H),
      IsPotent G → IsPotent H → IsPotent (Monoid.Coprod G H) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.1»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.1

by R. B. J. T. Allenby

A group $G$ is said to be *potent* if, to each $x \in G$ and each positive integer $n$
dividing the order of $x$ (we suppose $\infty$ is divisible by every positive integer),
there exists a finite homomorphic image of $G$ in which the image of $x$ has order
precisely $n$. Is the free product of two potent groups again potent?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped Monoid.Coprod

namespace Kourovka.«9.1»

universe u

/-- A group $G$ is *potent* if, to each $x \in G$ and each positive integer $n$ dividing the
order of $x$, there exists a finite homomorphic image of $G$ in which the image of $x$ has
order precisely $n$.

An element of infinite order has `orderOf x = 0`, and every `n` divides `0`, so this matches
the convention that $\infty$ is divisible by every positive integer. -/
def IsPotent (G : Type u) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : G) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → n ∣ orderOf x →
    ∃ (H : Type u) (_ : Group H) (_ : Finite H) (f : G →* H),
      Function.Surjective f ∧ orderOf (f x) = n

/-- The trivial group is potent. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPotent_of_subsingleton (G : Type u) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] : IsPotent G := by
  intro x n hn hdvd
  rw [Subsingleton.elim x 1, orderOf_one, Nat.dvd_one] at hdvd
  exact ⟨G, inferInstance, inferInstance, MonoidHom.id G, Function.surjective_id, by
    simp [hdvd, Subsingleton.elim x 1]⟩

/-- Every finite abelian group is potent. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPotent_of_finite_of_commGroup (G : Type u) [CommGroup G] [Finite G] : IsPotent G := by
  intro x n hn hdvd
  refine ⟨G ⧸ Subgroup.zpowers (x ^ n), inferInstance, inferInstance, QuotientGroup.mk' _,
    QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective _, ?_⟩
  rw [orderOf_eq_iff hn]
  refine ⟨?_, fun m hm hm0 h => ?_⟩
  · rw [← map_pow, QuotientGroup.mk'_apply, QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff]
    exact Subgroup.mem_zpowers _
  · rw [← map_pow, QuotientGroup.mk'_apply, QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff,
      Subgroup.mem_zpowers_iff] at h
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := h
    rw [← zpow_natCast, ← zpow_mul, ← zpow_natCast x m, zpow_eq_zpow_iff_modEq] at hk
    have h2 : (n : ℤ) ∣ (m : ℤ) := by
      have h3 : (n : ℤ) ∣ (m : ℤ) - n * k :=
        dvd_trans (Int.natCast_dvd_natCast.mpr hdvd) hk.dvd
      simpa using dvd_add h3 (dvd_mul_right (n : ℤ) k)
    exact absurd (Nat.le_of_dvd hm0 (Int.natCast_dvd_natCast.mp h2)) (not_le.mpr hm)

/-- Is the free product $G * H$ of two potent groups $G$ and $H$ again potent? -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.1» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H], IsPotent G → IsPotent H → IsPotent (G ∗ H) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.1»

/-!
# Conjecture 9.1

by R. B. J. T. Allenby

A group $G$ is said to be *potent* if, to each $x \in G$ and each positive integer $n$
dividing the order of $x$ (we suppose $\infty$ is divisible by every positive integer),
there exists a finite homomorphic image of $G$ in which the image of $x$ has order
precisely $n$. Is the free product of two potent groups again potent?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.1»

/--
A group $G$ is *potent* if, to each $x \in G$ and each positive integer $n$ dividing the
order of $x$ (where $\infty$ is divisible by every positive integer), there exists a finite
homomorphic image of $G$ in which the image of $x$ has order precisely $n$.

Here "$n$ divides the order of $x$" is `n ∣ orderOf x`; since Mathlib sets `orderOf x = 0`
for elements of infinite order and `n ∣ 0` for every `n`, this matches the convention that
$\infty$ is divisible by every positive integer. The restriction `0 < n` is the requirement
that $n$ be a *positive* integer.
-/
def IsPotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : G) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → n ∣ orderOf x →
    ∃ (K : Type) (_ : Group K) (_ : Finite K) (f : G →* K),
      Function.Surjective f ∧ orderOf (f x) = n

/-- The trivial group is potent. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPotent_unit : IsPotent Unit := by
  intro x n hn hdvd
  refine ⟨Unit, inferInstance, inferInstance, MonoidHom.id Unit, Function.surjective_id, ?_⟩
  rw [Subsingleton.elim x 1, orderOf_one, Nat.dvd_one] at hdvd
  simp [hdvd]

/--
Is the free product $G * H$ of two potent groups $G$ and $H$ again potent?

The free product of groups is Mathlib's coproduct `Monoid.Coprod G H`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.1» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H],
      IsPotent G → IsPotent H → IsPotent (Monoid.Coprod G H) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.1»

by R. B. J. T. Allenby

dividing the order of $x$ (we suppose $\infty$ is divisible by every positive integer),

open scoped Monoid.Coprod

namespace Kourovka.«9.1»

/--
A group $G$ is *potent* if, for each $x \in G$ and each positive integer $n$ dividing the
order of $x$, there is a finite homomorphic image of $G$ (a surjective homomorphism from $G$
onto a finite group) in which the image of $x$ has order precisely $n$.

An element of infinite order has `orderOf x = 0`, and every positive integer divides `0`,
which matches the convention that $\infty$ is divisible by every positive integer.
-/
def IsPotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : G) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → n ∣ orderOf x →
    ∃ (H : Type) (_ : Group H) (_ : Finite H) (f : G →* H),
      Function.Surjective f ∧ orderOf (f x) = n

/-- The trivial group is potent. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPotent_unit : IsPotent Unit := by
  intro x n hn hdvd
  have hx : orderOf x = 1 := orderOf_eq_one_iff.mpr (Subsingleton.elim _ _)
  rw [hx, Nat.dvd_one] at hdvd
  exact ⟨Unit, inferInstance, inferInstance, MonoidHom.id Unit, Function.surjective_id,
    hdvd ▸ hx⟩

/--
Is the free product of two potent groups again potent?

Here the free product $G * H$ is Mathlib's `Monoid.Coprod G H`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.1» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H], IsPotent G → IsPotent H → IsPotent (G ∗ H) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.1»
